# testdata

Sample certificates and keys for the tests and the demos. They are generated by
[`dev/gen-testdata`](../dev/gen-testdata/main.go) from a fixed seed (`task data:gen`), so the
files are byte-for-byte reproducible; CI regenerates them and fails on any difference.

The keys are weak on purpose. They protect nothing. Every certificate is signed by a throwaway
"Test CA" and uses names under `.example.test`.

| File | What it contains | Expected finding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `certs/ok-2048.pem`, `ok-2048.der` | 2048-bit key, e = 65537 (PEM and DER) | none |
| `certs/ok-4096.pem` | 4096-bit key | none |
| `certs/duplicate-of-ok-2048.pem` | another certificate for the `ok-2048` key | `duplicate-key` (high) |
| `certs/weak-512.pem` | 512-bit modulus | `key-size` (critical) |
| `certs/weak-1024.pem` | 1024-bit modulus | `key-size` (high) |
| `certs/weak-exponent-3.pem` | 2048-bit modulus, e = 3 | `public-exponent` (medium) |
| `certs/small-factor.pem` | modulus = 101 × a 2041-bit prime | `small-factor` (critical) |
| `certs/close-primes.pem` | two adjacent 1024-bit primes | `close-primes` (critical) |
| `certs/shared-prime-a.pem`, `shared-prime-b.pem` | two moduli sharing one 1024-bit prime | `shared-prime` (critical, both) |
| `certs/weak-sha1-signature.pem` | certificate signed with SHA-1 | `weak-signature` (medium) |
| `certs/expired.pem` | validity 2020-2021 | `expired` (low) |
| `certs/ecdsa-p256.pem` | ECDSA certificate | skipped (not RSA) |
| `keys/public-pkix-2048.pem` | `ok-2048` as a PKIX `PUBLIC KEY` | `duplicate-key` with `ok-2048` |
| `keys/public-pkcs1-4096.pem` | `ok-4096` as a PKCS#1 `RSA PUBLIC KEY` | `duplicate-key` with `ok-4096` |
